name: A1-03 HTTP Request - rate limits and back-off

meta.description: How to survive a 429. Spaces requests out with batching, retries on failure, and - the part most workflows get wrong - tells a retryable error apart from a permanent one instead of retrying both.
meta.author: Suyash Raj - https://rajsuyash.com/blog/n8n-error-handling-best-practices.html
meta.setup: None. httpbin.org returns whatever status code you ask it for, so the failure is reproducible on demand.
meta.expectedOutput: 'Call a rate-limited API' runs once per input item with a 1s gap every 5 items. 'Classify the failure' outputs one row per item with retryable: true for 429/500/502/503/504 and false for 400/401/403/404/422.
meta.failureCases: Change the status code in the Set node to 401 and watch 'Classify the failure' mark it permanent. That is the case where retrying is not resilience - it is three identical rejections and a three-times-longer outage before anyone is told.

nodes.name: Call a rate-limited API
nodes.notes: Three settings do three different jobs. batching spaces requests so you are less likely to be rate-limited at all. retryOnFail/maxTries/waitBetweenTries handle it when you are anyway. neverError + fullResponse stop the node throwing on a non-2xx, so the status code reaches the next node as data and you can decide what it means - which you cannot do if the node has already failed the execution.
